answer: Entropy-Fingerprint Audits: each agent periodically answers three micro-probes—knoll (CPU/clock jitter), ivory (DRAM timing), summit (network RTT)—using local hardware entropy and strict deadlines. Verifiers remove the common beacon and correlate residual vectors across identities. Duplicate agents on shared hosts/operators reveal correlated fingerprints, clustering them. To evade, an attacker must rent independent, low-correlation hardware and network paths per identity and keep timing separated; key copying alone fails, raising marginal cost per sybil.
